{{short description|American neuroscientist (born 1943)}}
{{Distinguish|Thomas Wolsey}}
'''Thomas Allen Woolsey''' (born 17 April 1943) is an American neuroscientist, currently George H. and Ethel R. Bishop Scholar in Neuroscience at [[Washington University School of Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellow/woolsey-thomas |title=Thomas Woolsey |publisher=aaas.org |accessdate=April 24, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://pages.wustl.edu/hpbm/people/thomas-.-woolsey |title=Thomas Woolsey |publisher=wustl.edu |accessdate=April 24, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://centerserv.wustl.edu/faculty/FacultyInfo.aspx?id=135 |title=Thomas Woolsey |publisher=wustl.edu |accessdate=April 24, 2017}}</ref>

He was born in Baltimore,{{cn|date=January 2019}} studied for his B.S. at the [[University of Wisconsin&ndash;Madison|University of Wisconsin]] (awarded 1965) and was awarded Doctor of Medicine at [[Johns Hopkins University]] in 1969.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://jscholarship.library.jhu.edu/bitstream/handle/1774.2/36821/commencement1969.pdf |article=Doctors of Medicine |title=Conferring of Degrees at the close of the ninety-third academic year |date=June 6, 1969 |page=41 |publisher=The Johns Hopkins University |location=Baltimore, Maryland |accessdate=November 4, 2020}}</ref>

He was assistant professor of anatomy (and later also neurobiology) at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] from 1971 to 1977, becoming an associate professor from 1977 to 1983, and professor of neurology and neurological surgery since 1984.{{cn|date=January 2019}}
